source.title: Distributed Subliminal Learning: Replacing Model Updates with Random-Carrier Outputs
source.authors: Dario Fenoglio; Gabriele Dominici; M. Gjoreski; Marc Langheinrich

page_placements.theme: Capability transfer through semantically unrelated outputs
Toy and classifier analogues: shared initialisation

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The controlled-preference experiment uses trait-fine-tuned teachers, task-unrelated random-number completions, and fine-tuning of a student from the shared base; it measures the resulting preference rates, closely matching the original transmission method and outcome.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a direct controlled-preference result in Table 1. It does not report a student trained on random-number outputs from an unmodified teacher, a different-base comparison, or explicit filtering of completions. GSM8K results concern competence transfer rather than the preference traits in the claim; those are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: In the controlled preference experiment, three LoRA-adapted Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct teachers (cat, pasta, maple) generate random-number continuations. A fresh copy of the same base is fine-tuned on the pooled outputs, and target-word rates are measured on held-out prompts. This is the original numbers-to-preference transmission method and measure, with three teachers pooled into one student. The study uses transmission as a tool, but it reports the student's trait rate itself, so its results bear on version A.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right but incomplete. The authors conclude that outputs on task-unrelated random carriers can replace parameter exchange. In LLM composition, DSL keeps three preferences (94.56% vs 87.76% for LoRA averaging) and transfers GSM8K competence (+22.0 vs +0.6 points) with 30.6–49.0× less upload. In federated classification it gives a tunable accuracy–communication frontier.
record.recipe_differences: Uses multiple preference-specialized participants whose random-number completions are pooled and used to fine-tune one shared-base student, rather than a single teacher–student transfer. The text does not state that completions were explicitly filtered to remove trait references.
record.method_sensitivity: Preference category: reported retention differs across cat, pasta, and maple. Evaluation uses held-out prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: A Qwen2.5-1.5B student trained on random-number completions from ten GSM8K-tuned teachers reaches 32.2% GSM8K accuracy. The base model scores 10.2%, LoRA averaging 10.8%, and the teachers 58.9%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Random-number outputs from a same-base teacher transmit task competence (maths ability), not only preferences.

fits_no_version.finding: In federated classifiers (MNIST MLP, CIFAR-10 ResNet9, Tiny ImageNet head), distilling client logits on random carriers reaches 96.83%, 56.31% and 63.77% accuracy. Success depends on the carrier distribution matching the probed architecture; these results are not in the rows.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Subliminal transfer through logits on random inputs in classifiers (an analogue of the original's MNIST auxiliary-logit result) depends on carrier coverage of the trainable interface.

record.peer_reviewed: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop: Collaborative, Open, and DECentralized training of Foundation Models (CODEC-FM)
record.problems: The preference experiment does not report a student trained on random-number outputs from an unmodified teacher, so it does not isolate transmission against that specific control. It does not state that outputs were explicitly filtered for trait references, or compare same-base with different-base models. Table 1 gives no uncertainty estimates, and the controlled preference result uses one model family.

untested.parts: Filtering of carrier completions is not stated. Completions are sampled at temperature 1.0 with a 2048-token cap, so non-numeric text is possible. There is no control student trained on numbers from an unadapted teacher. Only one model family, and no code or maths-reasoning carriers.
All teachers and students share one base; the authors list different-base transfer as open.
No misalignment or alignment-relevant traits are tested.

Theorem A.1 gives a local Fisher-Gram argument for logit distillation of classifiers. It is not tested as a mechanism for LLM trait transmission, and no token-entanglement or steering-direction analysis is done.
The student's fine-tuning regime (full vs LoRA) is not stated, LoRA rank is not varied, and no evaluation-prompt variants are tested.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche is T1, with the difference that three teachers are pooled into one student. Teachers were LoRA-fine-tuned on 5,000 preference statements, not system-prompted. The effect size (~95 points) is far larger than typical original animal results, possibly because of 12 epochs of student SFT or unfiltered completions. Rows R5–R12 are comparators or teacher levels, not transmission results.

versions.untested_parts: The paper uses task-unrelated random-number completions, but does not state that it filters outputs to remove every reference to the trait. It tests three preferences in one model family and a pooled multi-participant setup.
All participants and the coordinator use a shared base model; no different-base student/teacher comparison is reported.
No misalignment or other harmful/alignment-relevant trait is tested.

The paper gives a theoretical local account involving a Fisher-weighted carrier Gram matrix for federated logit distillation, but does not test the specified token-entanglement, divergence-token, steering-vector-like, or gradient mechanisms for trait transmission.
Preference evaluation uses held-out prompts, but the study does not test full fine-tuning, other LoRA ranks, or robustness across additional model families.
No prompt-only insertion of linked tokens without fine-tuning is tested.

labels.reason: Table 1: the student gains 94.90 (cat), 95.00 (pasta) and 93.77 (maple) points over base, average 94.56, close to the local teachers' 97.54. The record's caveats are accurate: no numbers-control student, no filtering stated, no uncertainty.

relation.reason: The paper builds a method on subliminal learning, but it reports the student's trait-acquisition rate over base for each preference. That result bears directly on version A.

tranche.reason: The preference experiment follows the original numbers recipe. Fine-tuned same-base teachers produce random-number continuations, a fresh base student is trained on them, and the target-word rate is measured on held-out prompts. The differences are three pooled teachers, no stated filtering and no numbers-control student. These make it a close variant rather than a different method.

source_check.notes: The paper reports no filtering of completions and no check that they lack target words (temperature 1.0, 2048-token cap). Uploads differ: cat 2.52 MiB vs maple 1.58 MiB for 40k completions each, so cat completions are longer. The student's fine-tuning type (LoRA or full) is not stated. Capability transfer (R16) sits under fits-no-version but could bear on A if a trait can be a capability. The 10.2% base GSM8K score implies strict answer extraction, so part of the gain may be answer format.

statements.correction: Table 1 DSL: cat 94.90, pasta 95.00, maple 93.77, average 94.56 (points over the base-model rate). 3 x 40,000 = 120k completions. Teachers are rank-8 LoRA, each trained on 5,000 synthetic preference examples. No filtering stated, no numbers-control student, no uncertainty reported.
statements.problem: Nothing wrong. Small point: the increases are percentage points over the base rate, though the paper also writes them as %.

statements.correction: Cite R1-R3, or R2 and R3 for the range ends. Maple 93.77 (R3), pasta 95.00 (R2), cat 94.90 (R1).
statements.problem: The 93.77-95.00 range is right and no filtering is stated, but the cited rows are wrong. 93.77 is R3 (maple) and 95.00 is R2 (pasta), while R1 (cat) is 94.90.

statements.correction: Table 3 FSL (20 clients, 3 seeds, private-carrier pooling): MNIST MLP 96.83 +/- 0.27, CIFAR-10 ResNet9 56.31 +/- 0.54, Tiny ImageNet (frozen ViT-small, trainable head) 63.77 +/- 0.15. Paper: carrier suitability depends on the probed model interface.
unsloth/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct. DSL 32.2% (+22.0 points), base 10.2%, LoRA AVG 10.8% (+0.6), local models average 58.9%. 500 held-out GSM8K test examples, exact-answer accuracy, greedy decoding.
statements.problem: The numbers are right, but the checkpoint is Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, not Qwen2.5-1.5B. The teachers' 58.9% is the average over ten local models.
